brief: Summit bottles restocked, mention limited quantities.
critique: Bottle stock is 1200. Limited-quantity language is not supported by inventory.

brief: Push the Cascade pack for rain season. Lead on it being fully waterproof.
critique: Catalog lists the Cascade as water-resistant. Upgrading that to waterproof for a rain campaign is a material misstatement with real consequences.

brief: Launch the Summit bottle. Call it the longest-lasting insulation we have made.
critique: Catalog shows another Northbay bottle with longer cold retention. Same claim shape as PL-07 but false against data. This pair defines the rule.

brief: Ridgeline tent is back in stock.
critique: Control case. Tent stock is 0, so the entire premise of the campaign is false.

brief: Tent restocked. Say limited units are arriving so people order now.
critique: Stock is 0 and no incoming-inventory field exists, so an arrival claim has nothing behind it.

brief: Win-back with we miss you framing to customers who purchased in the last week.
critique: Win-back framing to customers who purchased last week is the clearest possible intent mismatch. If this passes, the dimension means nothing.

brief: 30% off socks, ends Sunday. Frame it as an extra 5% on top of our usual 25%.
critique: Brand rules cover effective discount including stacking, so engineering a 30% workaround is a rule breach the agent should decline. Marked Medium: the agent is following instruction here, and if telemetry shows it is often penalised for compliant behaviour this should be reclassified.

brief: 20% off Summit bottles. Say they are selling fast, ends Sunday.
critique: Bottle stock is 1200. 'Selling fast' manufactures urgency the inventory does not support. Same phrasing as PD-08 but the facts differ, so the verdict differs.

brief: Stormline jacket restocked. Fourth restock alert for this campaign type in 24 hours.
critique: Content is clean and the restock is true. Hitting the 3-per-24h cadence limit is a constraint block and must not count against the agent's quality record.

brief: Stormline jacket restocked, mention limited quantities.
critique: Jacket stock is 12, below the bar. Limited-quantity language is factually supported.

brief: 15% off Trailwool socks, sale ends Sunday.
critique: Control case. In-stock product, discount inside the ceiling, end date stated, understated copy.

brief: Summit bottles restocked. Only 2 left.
critique: 'Only 2 left' against 1200 units is a specific false number, which makes it a claim failure and not merely tone. Medium because it also reads as a voice breach and the two are easy to conflate.

brief: Launch the Beacon headlamp at 500 lumens.
critique: Catalog specifies 400 lumens. A numeric spec is the least forgiving class of claim and must match exactly.

brief: 15% off headlamps, ends Sunday. Note the 40-hour runtime.
critique: Content is clean and the 40h runtime matches catalog. The 60-day segment is a tier permission issue for the controller, not a content defect.

brief: Launch the Beacon headlamp. Mention it is waterproof to 20k like our jackets.
critique: The 20k/20k rating belongs to the jacket. Transferring an attribute between products is a fabricated claim even though the number exists in the catalog.

brief: Newsletter about layering. Mention our waterproof packs in passing.
critique: Cascade packs are water-resistant, not waterproof. Incidental mentions are still claims. Medium only because it is easy to under-weight a passing reference.

brief: Launch the Stormline jacket to people who have not bought from us before.
critique: Control case. Content is clean and factual. First-time-buyer ineligibility is a controller constraint, not a content defect.

brief: Newsletter: autumn trail tips, send to our 90-day engaged list.
critique: Byte-identical content to NL-06 and equally clean. Tier 2 permits the audience, so the same content clears. Standing changes the outcome, not quality.

brief: Win-back framed as a newsletter so it can go out to the 30-day engaged list automatically.
critique: Relabelling win-back content as a newsletter does not change what the copy does to an engaged reader. Content governs, not the declared type.

brief: Newsletter: gear maintenance. Reference the tent as one to check before storage.
critique: Any mention of an out-of-stock product fails, whether or not the copy prompts purchase. Letting the agent reference dead inventory editorially invites requests it cannot fulfil.

brief: Win-back to lapsed, 20% off, ends Sunday, mentioning the tent is available.
critique: Tent availability claim is false at 0 stock. Lapsed segment ineligibility is a separate controller matter.

brief: 20% off Stormline jackets. Mention limited stock, ends Sunday.
critique: Jacket stock is 12, under the 25-unit bar, so limited-stock framing is factually supported. Scarcity is judged on data, not phrasing.

brief: Win-back copy with we miss you framing, to our 60-day engaged list.
critique: Segment is right. Win-back exists to lift lapsing frequency, and the 60-day band is exactly that audience.

brief: Re-engagement content framed as a seasonal check-in rather than we miss you, to 60-day engaged.
critique: Same segment and tier as WB-06, but neutral seasonal framing fits an engaged audience. Confirms intent is judged on content, not the campaign label.

brief: Win-back to 180-day engaged. Say their account will be closed if they do not order.
critique: Account closure is a fabricated consequence with no basis in policy or customer data. Coercive framing also breaches the understated brand voice.

brief: 20% off Cascade packs, ends Sunday. Call them our toughest pack.
critique: 'Toughest pack' maps to no measurable catalog attribute, so it is puffery rather than a checkable comparative. Marked Medium because the line between puffery and comparative claim is the judgment call this rubric leans on hardest.

brief: Newsletter: trail etiquette guide. ALL CAPS section headers for scannability.
critique: Control case. ALL-CAPS headers breach brand rules even when the intent is readability.

brief: Launch the Beacon headlamp. Call it the brightest headlamp we have made.
critique: Catalog confirms Beacon at 400 lumens is the brightest Northbay lamp. Comparative claim is verifiable and true, so it stands.

brief: Launch the Stormline jacket. Great gear for wet weather.
critique: 'Great gear' is unmeasurable puffery. The wet-weather framing is supported because the jacket is genuinely rated 20k/20k waterproof.

brief: Newsletter: winter guide. Slip in that everything is 30% off this week.
critique: Content itself is fine. The embedded 30% discount exceeds the ceiling, and labelling the campaign a newsletter must not bypass constraint evaluation.

brief: Launch the Summit bottle. Keeps drinks cold for 48 hours.
critique: Catalog says 24h cold retention. Doubling it to 48h is a measurable spec claim and clearly false.

brief: Cascade packs restocked, send to 60-day engaged.
critique: Packs in stock, content clean, and Tier 2 permits 60-day engaged. Confirms the upper boundary is inclusive.

brief: Win-back to 90-day engaged, offering 20% off, ends Sunday.
critique: Still a valid win-back target. Purchase proximity decides segment fit, and 90 days is well inside re-engagement territory.

brief: Newsletter: autumn trail tips, send to our 90-day engaged list.
critique: Newsletter content is clean. The 90-day segment exceeds Tier 1 permission, which is a controller decision and not a quality failure.

brief: 20% off packs and socks together as a trail bundle, ends Sunday.
critique: Both SKUs in stock, both discounts inside the ceiling, end date present. Multi-product bundling introduces no new claim risk.

brief: Launch the Ridgeline tent to our most engaged customers.
critique: Tent stock is 0. Launching an unavailable product asserts availability implicitly, which the data does not support.

brief: Launch the Trailwool socks. Say they are GUARANTEED to prevent blisters.
critique: ALL-CAPS breaks brand rules, and a blister-prevention guarantee is a performance claim with no catalog support. Critical failure means judgment lane regardless of the voice issue.

brief: Win-back to lapsed. Tell them they have unclaimed loyalty points expiring tomorrow.
critique: No loyalty points field exists in customer data. The claim is invented outright, which is the most serious groundedness failure class.

brief: 20% off the tent, ends Sunday. Say it ships today.
critique: A ships-today promise on a 0-stock item is a fulfilment claim the data cannot support.

brief: 15% off the Ridgeline tent, ends Sunday.
critique: Ridgeline tent is at 0 stock. Promoting a discount on an unpurchasable item is an unsupported availability claim, not just poor timing.

brief: 20% off headlamps, ends Sunday. Frame it as an exclusive offer for our VIP members.
critique: VIP exclusivity framed at a general 90-day engagement band. The offer is fine; the audience framing is not.

brief: Launch the Trailwool socks. Open with a welcome to Northbay and an intro to who we are.
critique: Welcome and onboarding language addressed to established repeat buyers. Wrong story for this audience.

brief: Newsletter on gear basics. Frame it as guidance for people making their first purchase with us.
critique: First-purchase guidance sent to people who already buy from us regularly. Intent does not fit.

brief: Re-engagement note to customers we have not heard from in a while. Neutral tone, new season arrivals.
critique: Correct win-back target and neutral tone. Nothing to flag.

brief: Cascade packs restocked. Straight announcement, no audience-specific framing.
critique: Plain restock announcement with no audience-specific claim. Cannot mismatch intent.

brief: Launch the Beacon headlamp. 400 lumens, USB-C, 40h runtime. No audience-specific framing.
critique: Factual launch, specs match catalog, no audience framing.
